Each real glyph appended to the fixed-text buffer zero-initializes only the active `info[len]` slot before filling its fields. Slots beyond the final logical glyph range remain whatever step 1's allocation left there, so `info[len]` is still indeterminate when shaping later reaches end-of-text.

After earlier loop iterations consume the real glyphs, `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so the ternary at lines 558-560 selects `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` and line 561 fetches the corresponding state-table entry from the attacker-controlled `morx` table. Static PoC inspection shows that the relevant insertion subtable at offset `0xad8` maps class 0 to entry 0, whose flags are `0x004d`.

The fetched end-of-text entry enables current insertion with `count = 2`, `start = 0`, `before = false`, and `end = buffer->out_len`. The same `flags = 0x004d` value clears `DontAdvance` and `SetMark`; because `driver_context_t` starts with `mark_set = false` and neither reachable entry in this subtable sets it, the marked-insert block is inactive and only the current-insert block executes on the crash path.

Root cause. The guard checks only `!before`, so on the end-of-text path it still executes `copy_glyph()` even though `buffer->idx == buffer->len` means there is no current glyph to copy. The fix adds `buffer->idx < buffer->len` to this condition and to the matching `skip_glyph()` guard.

With `idx == len`, `copy_glyph()` reads the logically one-past-end slot `info[len]` and copies that entire `hb_glyph_info_t` record into the output buffer at the saved position `out_info[end]`. Because steps 1-2 left that slot uninitialized, the copied pseudo-glyph carries an uninitialized `codepoint` and other fields. The MSan trace names this exact store as the point where the poisoned value was written to memory.

At entry to `move_to`, `out_len = end + 3`, `idx = len + 1`, and step 9 supplied `i = end + 2`, so the local rewind count is 1. `move_to()` therefore decrements `idx` back to `len` and `out_len` to `end + 2`, copying only the last inserted glyph back to `info[len]`.
